text:
yuki: Heads up — on archipelago-v1 int4 bring-up I’m seeing a weird combo failure for mixed vertical Japanese (ruby/furigana) interleaved with Arabic snippets. Translation BLEU drops ~3.8 pts vs fp16 in our smoke. Samples attached below.

sam: ugh, can you paste a minimal repro output?

yuki: sure. input: "漢字(ふりがな) and العربية: ١٢٣"
output fp16: "漢字(ふりがな) と العربية: ١٢٣"
output int4: "漢字ふりがな) と ءالعربية: 123"
(note the missing paren and the arabic word gets a stray hamza + western digits)

anish: that looks like both a tokenization boundary and bidi/punct mirror problem. likely two layers: subtokens shuffled then post-processing detok sees different rune order.

lena: any BLEU / embed numbers?

yuki: BLEU fp16=32.1, int4=28.3 on our small L10k test. Embedding cosine on reference vs output: fp16 0.924, int4 0.872. Also hallucination rate up for numerics.

sam: hmm — run token-level inspection with --show-tokens and dump byte offsets? could be tokenizer vocab split changed when quant kernels reorder attention?

anish: please run:

```
python eval/run_translate.py \
  --model archipelago-v1.int4 \
  --input samples/mixed_vertical_arabic.txt \
  --show-tokens --output out/int4.debug.txt
```

then same for archipelago-v1.fp16 and diff.

yuki: started that now. attaching snippets from --show-tokens (int4):

```
# token stream (int4)
漢字 ( ふ り が な )  と  ﻻ  العرب  ية  :  1 2 3
# token stream (fp16)
漢字 ( ふ り が な )  と  العربية : ١٢٣
```

anish: look at the ﻻ vs العربية split — it seems the arabic ligature got split and a run of latin digits replaced. That suggests a detokenization or unicode normalisation divergence in the int4 path. Any kernel-time normalization hooks?

lena: we did a change in tokenization preproc for speed in the int4 runtime last week — it toggles NFKC on some flows to collapse widths. @anish maybe that interacts with ZWJ/ZWSP around ruby markers?

anish: good catch. @yuki can you run the same input with runtime flag --no-unicode-normalize and also try quant backend=qkernel-v2 vs qkernel-v1?

ml-ci-bot: job started: eval/archipelago/int4/mixed_vertical_arabic/run-2026-03-21-1756 (link: https://ci.local/runs/12345) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-deploy-bot: reminder: int4 canary on staging rolling, keep an eye on latency SLOs.

yuki: ran both. With --no-unicode-normalize int4 output aligns with fp16 (paren preserved, arabic word intact) and embedding cos jumps to 0.918. With qkernel-v1 vs v2 there's a small token boundary diff but normalization seems to be the main factor.

sam: so root cause = toggled unicode normalization in the int4 preproc path. We should revert or gate it behind locale-aware heuristics.

anish: agree. quick mitigation: disable unicode normalization for inputs containing CJK ruby markers (U+303B.. range?) or Arabic script ranges, and add a regression test to eval-suite. Also add a token-stream diff check to CI that fails on >0.5% token-ops mismatch for multilingual tests.

lena: can you open a PR with the revert + tests? tag me and @ml-team for review. We should also add a canary metric for "multiscript-token-mismatch" in console.

yuki: will do. created a minimal repro gist and put outputs in the run artifacts.

sam: thanks — good catch. once PR merges we should re-run the full L10k run and bump archipelago int4 canary if stable.

anish: follow-up — add a short note in the onboarding doc about runtime normalization differences for quant backends (so future bring-ups avoid this).

ml-ci-bot: eval job finished: status=partial-fail, details at https://ci.local/runs/12345/logs

ops-deploy-bot: canary paused until archipelago-int4 normalization revert is in staging. :pause_button:
